issues.legal_issue: A Hindu widow who reacquires the same property she had transferred before the relevant legal change becomes its full owner when the transfer is reversed and her original interest is restored.
material_facts: The widow inherited a limited estate in the property from her husband and transferred it before the Hindu Succession Act came into force.
After the Act came into force, the transferee reconveyed the same property to the widow, restoring the interest she had previously transferred.
When her title was challenged, she had reacquired and was possessed of the property.
issues.conclusion: The widow became the full owner of the property under Section 14(1), and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act provides that property possessed by a female Hindu, whether acquired before or after the Act commenced, is held by her as full owner and not as a limited owner. The Explanation includes property acquired by purchase or in any other manner. Section 4 displaces inconsistent prior Hindu law. The Court approved Chinnakolandai Goundan v. Thanji Gounder, Teja Singh v. Jagat Singh, Ramgowda Aunagowda v. Bhausaheb, and Champa v. Chandrakant; it overruled Ganesh Mahanta v. Sukria Bewa and Medicherla Venkataratnam v. Siddani Palamma. Kotturuswamy v. Veeravva was distinguished because the widow there had obtained possession as a trespasser without title.

rule.if: property_title_appeal and female_had_limited_inherited_interest and female_transferred_property_before_legal_change and transferee_reconveyed_same_property_to_her and reconveyance_restored_original_interest and female_lawfully_held_property_when_title_was_challenged

predicates.property_title_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a disputed claim to ownership of property.
predicates.female_had_limited_inherited_interest: A female Hindu inherited a limited interest in the property from her husband.
predicates.female_transferred_property_before_legal: The female Hindu transferred the property before the legal change that abolished limited ownership of such property.
predicates.transferee_reconveyed_same_property_to_h: The transferee later transferred the same property back to the female Hindu.
predicates.reconveyance_restored_original_interest: The return transfer reversed the earlier transaction and restored the interest the female Hindu had transferred.
predicates.female_lawfully_held_property_when_title: The female Hindu had lawfully reacquired and held the property when her title was challenged.

issues.definition: If a property-title appeal concerns a female Hindu who inherited a limited interest, transferred the property before the legal change, later received the same property back through a transaction restoring her original interest, and lawfully held it when her title was challenged, she holds it as full owner.

issues.legal_issue: A female Hindu need not have physical or constructive possession of property when the relevant legal change takes effect if she has acquired and possesses a legal interest in it when her title is challenged.
material_facts: The widow was not in possession of the property when the Hindu Succession Act came into force because she had previously transferred it.
The transferee later reconveyed the property to her, and she had reacquired and was possessed of it when her title was challenged.
issues.conclusion: Possession, physical or constructive, at the commencement of the Act was not a prerequisite to full ownership; possession in the legal sense when title is called into question is sufficient, provided the property was lawfully acquired.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) applies to property possessed by a female Hindu whether acquired before or after the Act commenced. The Court interpreted “possessed of” as referring to a right or interest in the property, rather than requiring physical possession at commencement. Kotturuswamy v. Veeravva was distinguished because possession obtained by trespass without title was not a lawful acquisition.

predicates.property_title_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a disputed claim to ownership of property.
predicates.female_acquired_property: A female Hindu acquired an interest in the property by a lawful means.
predicates.female_had_legal_possession_when_title_w: The female Hindu had a legal right or interest in the property when her title was challenged, even if she lacked physical or constructive possession when the relevant legal change took effect.

issues.definition: If an appeal concerns property acquired by a female Hindu and she had a legal interest in it when her title was challenged, she holds the property as full owner even if she lacked physical or constructive possession when the legal change took effect.

issues.legal_issue: A reversioner’s future chance of succession does not defeat a widow’s full ownership when a transfer of her property is reversed and the property is restored to her.
material_facts: The widow temporarily transferred property in which she had inherited a limited estate.
The transferee later reconveyed that property to her, reversing the earlier transaction and restoring her interest.
The competing reversioner had only a possible future chance of succeeding to the property.
issues.conclusion: The reversal of the transaction did not affect any existing right of the reversioner, whose mere expectancy could not defeat the widow’s full ownership.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that a reversioner has only a spes successionis, or chance of future succession, and that this expectancy is not a present right in the property. When the transaction is reversed and the widow’s interest is restored, Section 14(1) applies to enlarge that interest into full ownership.

rule.if: property_title_appeal and widow_had_limited_interest and same_property_was_restored_to_widow and reversioner_had_only_future_succession_expectancy

predicates.property_title_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a disputed claim to ownership of property.
predicates.widow_had_limited_interest: A widow held a limited interest in the property before transferring it.
predicates.same_property_was_restored_to_widow: The property the widow transferred was later returned to her, reversing the earlier transaction.
predicates.reversioner_had_only_future_succession_e: The competing reversioner had only a possible future chance of succession and no present right to the property.

issues.definition: If a property-title appeal concerns a widow whose transferred property is restored to her and the competing reversioner has only a future succession expectancy, that expectancy cannot defeat the widow’s full ownership.
